column1: # scripts/retracted-claims.tsv - THE retraction ledger, as data
# One row per retracted, superseded, or premise-invalidated claim. This file is
# the single authority; docs/CLAIMS_REGISTER.md is the prose index that points
# here. It exists as TSV rather than prose for three reasons:
#   1. It can be CHECKED. scripts/check-retracted-claims.sh reads it and fails
#      when a ledger pattern is asserted in a script or doc without a retraction
#      marker nearby.
#   2. It can be DIFFED. Adding a retraction is a one-line append, visible in
#      review as a row, not a paragraph rewrite.
#   3. It can be COUNTED. This file is the ONLY source of the retraction count.
#      THE RETRACTION COUNT IS THE NUMBER OF ROWS WHOSE STATUS IS `refuted`.
#      `superseded` is excluded (the claim was true and is now old) and
#      `invalidated-premise` is excluded (the ledger says in terms that this
#      "IS NOT a retraction"). Print all three numbers with:
#          scripts/check-retracted-claims.sh --count
#      This project carried FOUR prose counts of its own retractions and no two
#      agreed: "doze" in docs/RE_CITY_FREEZE.md, "eleven" in
#      docs/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md and in check-retracted-claims.sh's own header,
#      "These eight" in docs/CLAIMS_REGISTER.md section 1, and "13 commits"
#      counted off git log. All four were wrong the same way - each was a human
#      tally of a moving target. On 2026-10-02 all four were removed and
#      `check-retracted-claims.sh` grew a section that FAILS when any prose
#      count disagrees with the number computed here. Prose that states no count
#      is always fine, so appending a row here never breaks a document.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated):
#   id       stable identifier, cited by decisions and tickets
#   kind     token | phrase      (token = case-sensitive, phrase = case-insensitive)
#   status   refuted | superseded | invalidated-premise
#   pattern  the literal string to look for
#   where    file:line where the retraction lives. Checked for existence.
# STATUS SEMANTICS - the distinction is load-bearing:
#   refuted              A measurement showed the claim to be false.
#   superseded           The claim was true and has been replaced by a later
#                        measurement. It is not wrong, it is old.
#   invalidated-premise  The claim's EVIDENCE was refuted. The inference is
#                        therefore void. THE CLAIM'S TRUTH IS UNKNOWN. This is
#                        NOT a retraction, and a checker that treats it as one
#                        will replace an unmeasured assertion with an
#                        unmeasured assertion of the opposite sign. That is
#                        exactly how the paired $0B51 retraction happened.
# R-034 (2026-10-02) is the second claim retracted in two languages (R-005..R-008
# was the first). The English original was in
# docs/measurements/2026-10-02-t093-peer-0B51-writer.md and the Portuguese mirror
# in docs/RE_CITY_FREEZE.md section 5. The checker caught the mirror on its own:
# seeding R-034 turned check-claims red at RE_CITY_FREEZE.md:4076 while the
# English page already carried a marker. That is the guard working, and it is the
# argument for keeping the ledger over hand-editing each document - the same
# retraction had to be written twice by hand and the ledger made the second write
# a gate failure rather than a silent divergence.
# KNOWN CEILING ON THE COUNT, stated rather than left to be discovered:
# two `refuted` rows retract the SAME claim in two languages (R-005/R-006
# English/Portuguese, R-007/R-008 likewise), so the refuted row count is an
# UPPER BOUND on the number of DISTINCT retracted claims. This file records no
# claim identity, and inventing one to make the number prettier would be
# judgement dressed as data.
# R-028..R-030 (2026-10-02) are the first rows added for a claim that no gate had
# caught: "the Deck cannot build this project", false since 9624f0e. The rootfs
# damage it rested on is REAL and still true - 503 of 504 glibc headers are absent
# from disk while pacman reports the package installed. The headers came from
# archive.archlinux.org into /home/deck/sysroot with -idirafter. So the diagnosis
# was right and the inference drawn from it was wrong, which is the same shape as
# the paired $0B51 retraction: a correct observation carrying an unsupported
# conclusion. See docs/CONFLICTS.md CONF-2 and aes/decisions/D009.md.
# WHEN YOU RETRACT SOMETHING: append a row. Do not edit prose to remove the
# claim, and do not weaken a pattern to make a check pass.
# id          kind     status                 pattern                                       where
